transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-21 15:00 PST
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Jared Kim, Priya Natarajan, Lena Ortiz (Redwood) - Marta Ruiz, Elliot Cheng, Samir Patel, Olivia Hart (Granite Bank)

Optional auto-generated: Summary present, action items listed

[00:00] Jared: Hey everyone thanks for joining, looks like we have a full house. Quick intro, I'm Jared on the AE side, Priya is our solutions engineer, Lena is your CSM. Marta, do you want to kick with a quick recap of your goals?

[00:15] Marta: Sure, thanks Jared. We're trying to scope a POC to validate serving a conversational assistant inside our mobile banking app. Main concerns are latency during the peak morning window, cost predictability, and of course data residency and audit logs. We gave you a high level of traffic but want Redwood to help translate that into capacity and SLA ask.

[00:35] Jared: Great. Priya, want to take us through what we'll need for workload thermography?

[00:40] Priya: Yeah so the first thing is request trace — timestamps, request size, response length distribution. Ideally a week of traffic, sanitized. From your note we saw baseline QPS around 10-15, but you mentioned some bursts up to two to three hundred? Wanted to confirm.

[01:05] Elliot: Right so current prod graph shows baseline 12 QPS, typical concurrency around 18, but our peak events — like morning auth and promos — spike to 180 to 230 QPS for short windows, around 90 to 120 seconds. That causes retries and longer tails.

[01:25] Priya: That helps. For modeling we separate steady-state QPS from burst topology. For steady-state we'd size for 12 QPS with concurrency 20ish; for burst we look at 200 QPS transient with concurrency approaching 60 to 80 depending on token lengths.

[01:45] Marta: Token lengths: most of our prompts are short — 20 to 60 input tokens — but model completions average 220 to 320 tokens because the assistant gives contextual steps. We saw in a sample that the output often gets long if user asks for step-by-step.

[02:05] Jared: So to confirm, concurrency metric we want to use is in-flight requests (open streams) not just QPS, because of long outputs. Priya, can you remind them about KV cache and prefix caching effect on throughput?

[02:25] Priya: Absolutely. If you can cache user context (prefix caching) and warm KV cache for common templates, effective tokens per request drop and latency improves. For the POC we'll run both cold and warmed cache scenarios. Note: our autotuner will recommend batching thresholds but for interactive flows we keep batching small to preserve latency.

[02:50] Olivia: Quick Sec question — Samir, do you want to ask about KMS and logs?

[02:55] Samir: Yeah, we need to know what keys are customer-managed, how audit logs are retained, and whether we can require TLS mTLS to Dedicated nodes. Also SOC two evidence and ISO are must-haves.

[03:15] Lena: We'll send the security pack — SOC 2 attestation, network diagrams, KMS options (bring-your-own and Redwood-managed), and our retention policies. Priya will attach notes on on-prem-ish VPC peering options.

[03:30] Marta: Good. Back to metrics — what should our success criteria look like at the end of the POC?

[03:35] Priya: From our experience, make them be measurable: 1) P99 gen latency under X (we suggested 350ms for your interactive target), 2) SLO for availability 99.9% during test windows, 3) throughput support for peak bursts without >1% error rate, 4) cost per 1k tokens within your budget envelope. If you want stricter latency we can try Dedicated with more aggressive batching and quantization.

[04:05] Elliot: If we go Dedicated, what are the quantization tradeoffs? We care about output quality for financial guidance.

[04:12] Priya: Quantization (8-bit/4-bit) can reduce memory and increase throughput but sometimes introduces subtle quality regression. For finance intents we recommend running evals on your prompt set; Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profile per model. We'll include a quality regression test in the bench plan.

[04:35] Jared: Let's put tentative numbers on the board. Baseline: 12 QPS, concurrency 20, avg input tokens 40, avg output tokens 260. Burst: target synthetic test at 200 QPS sustained for 90s, concurrency spike to 70, tail latency P99 target 350ms. Is that acceptable as a starting point?

[04:58] Marta: That matches our internal calculations, yes. We'll aim to produce sanitized traces that show those bursts.

[05:10] Priya: Benchmark plan — four-week pilot suggested: Week 0 (prep) data ingestion and replay tooling; Week 1 (baseline runs) run steady-state replay and confirm config; Week 2 (burst tests) run controlled bursts and tail profiling; Week 3 (retrospective) compile results, model/quantization recommendations and cost estimate; Week 4 decision and optional roll-forward. We can compress to three weeks if Granite is ready with traces.

[05:40] Elliot: For the replay tooling, what do you need format-wise?

[05:44] Priya: CSV or newline json with timestamp, request_id, prompt_len_tokens, expected_response_len_tokens, metadata (anonymized user cohort). We'll provide a template. Also we prefer to get typical success/failure rates to reproduce error handling.

[06:05] Samir: About networking — will we need a VPC peering for the Dedicated pilot or is a private endpoint enough?

[06:10] Priya: We support both. For strict isolation and mTLS we recommend VPC peering for the Dedicated capacity trial. For hosted pilot we can do private endpoints + strict egress rules. We'll note tradeoffs in the security doc.

[06:30] Jared: Budget question — Marta, Olivia, you mentioned a target monthly spend for POC?

[06:35] Olivia: We have a provisional budget for the pilot, roughly equivalent to two mid-size GPU months. We want an estimate though — per-token cost and Dedicated seat monthly.

[06:45] Priya: We'll produce a cost projection alongside the bench report, showing per-1000-token costs across steady and burst scenarios and a blended monthly projection. Also show sensitivity to quantization and batching.

[07:00] Marta: On success criteria, also include quality gates: mean BLEU-ish for template match, and no unsupported hallucinations for regulatory Q&A. We'll share a small test set for that.

[07:10] Priya: Good call — include a small labeled prompt set to run regression tests post-quantization. We'll run automatic checks and flag any deltas.

[07:25] Jared: Logistics and timeline recap — can we commit to the following: you (Granite) provide traces by 2026-11-25; we run baseline and burst in the week starting 2026-11-30; Redwood delivers report by 2026-12-10; decision meeting week of 2026-12-14. Sound right?

[07:50] Marta: Yes that works, assuming we can hit the trace scrub deadline.

[08:00] Samir: We'll start security review in parallel, but expect follow-ups about data-in-transit and KMS separation.

[08:08] Priya: Noted. Also small note — if you plan to enable tool-calling or function-style responses, that changes token patterns a bit; include that in the tracer if possible.

[08:25] Elliot: We'll add a marker for function calls in the trace.

[08:30] Olivia: Are there any competitors we should be aware of that Redwood sees in the enterprise banking space?

[08:35] Jared: Some customers evaluate SageCloud and a few infra vendors like Infera. For banks, the differentiators are VPC/on-prem options and auditable log streams. We'll compare in the follow-up deck.

[08:50] Marta: Last question — what's the risk that during the burst tests we see model OOM or kv cache thrash?

[08:58] Priya: If tokens-per-request are large and concurrency spikes, OOM risk increases without proper quantization and kernel selection. That's why we plan kernel/compilation profiles and will advise on model shard size. We'll also run memory-pressure scenarios to identify thresholds.

[09:20] Jared: Great. I'm going to summarize next steps and owners.

[09:25] Jared: Action items: Jared send bench template and replay tool; Marta provide traces; Priya schedule bench kickoff; Samir review security pack. We'll attach a checklist in follow-up email.

[09:40] Marta: Thanks all. Looking forward to the test.

[09:46] Jared: Thanks, meeting adjourned.

(End of transcript)

Notes on transcript quality: auto transcription had several mis-hearings around product names ("Redwood Dedicate" vs "Redwood Dedicated"), some numeric tokens mis-transcribed in the first pass; we validated numbers during the call.
